name: World War I and the Occupation of Galicia (1914–1917) (C0070)

techniques.comment: The mass deportation of the civilian population of occupied Galicia: "The Greek Catholic clergy suffered particular persecution. On September 18, 1914, Metropolitan A. Sheptytsky was arrested and taken away to Russia. In all, thousands of Galicians were removed as hostages (through Kyiv alone about 12 thousand passed)"(Citation: Енциклопедія історії України: Т. 8 2011).

The forced conscription of millions into the imperial army: "During the war years, 3.5 million Ukrainians were mobilized into the ranks of the Russian army (by other data – 4.5 million out of a total of 15.5 million)"(Citation: Енциклопедія історії України: Т. 8 2011).

The purge of Ukrainian institutions and the persecution of the movement's leaders. Hrushevsky was "arrested by the gendarmerie in Kyiv on December 11, 1914, and accused of Austrophilia and involvement in creating the Legion of Ukrainian Sich Riflemen. He was sent into exile to Simbirsk"(Citation: Енциклопедія історії України: Т. 2 2004), then transferred to Kazan with a teaching ban and stripped of his professorship.
